This guide is for package authors who know S4 classes and method dispatch.
Start with the [workflow guide](Workflow.html) ([source](https://github.com/luciu5/antitrust/blob/master/vignettes/Workflow.Rmd)) for ordinary model use.

There are two things an extension must keep straight: the **economic model**
that determines demand and firm behavior, and the **lifecycle** that takes
that model from observed data to a fitted market and then to a
counterfactual result. `antitrust` uses its established S4 model classes for
the economics and provides a common lifecycle for asking new questions of a
fit. The [workflow vignette](Workflow.html) ([source](https://github.com/luciu5/antitrust/blob/master/vignettes/Workflow.Rmd)) shows that lifecycle in use; the
[models vignette](Models.html) ([source](https://github.com/luciu5/antitrust/blob/master/vignettes/Models.Rmd)) explains the economics behind it.

## Objects in the lifecycle

```text
model_spec() + observed inputs  --calibrate()-->  AntitrustFit
model_spec() + known parameters --specify()---->  AntitrustFit
AntitrustFit + Counterfactual --simulate()---->  model S4 result (one step)
AntitrustFit + multiple steps --simulate()----->  CounterfactualPath
```

`model_spec()` identifies one supported combination of demand, conduct, and
variant. Both `calibrate()` and `specify()` return an `AntitrustFit`, a
subclass of `StructuralFit`. It holds the model identity, the fitted S4
object, structural parameters, observed inputs, and diagnostics. This is the
state of the market *before* a proposed change.

A `Counterfactual` holds one or more `CounterfactualStep` objects. For a
single step, `simulate()` returns the usual model result class, such as
`Logit`, `CES`, `Cournot`, or `Auction2ndLogit`. With several steps it returns
a `CounterfactualPath`; `result_at()` and `final_result()` retrieve the
model results along that path.

Returning the established result classes preserves their methods for prices,
elasticities, welfare, and other outputs. It also lets auctions, quantity
games, and bargaining retain the results that make sense for each model.
`summary(fit)` describes stored fitted state; `summary(result)` uses the
result class's method to describe a simulation.

## S4 relationships that affect behavior

Inheritance is useful for finding shared storage and method dispatch, but it
does not by itself tell you which economic equation a class solves. The map
below shows the main relationships. Indentation means “extends”; omitted
descendants do not affect the lifecycle described here.

```text
StructuralFit (virtual)
  └─ AntitrustFit

Antitrust
  ├─ Bertrand
  │   ├─ Linear
  │   │   ├─ LogLin
  │   │   └─ AIDS ── PCAIDS ── PCAIDSNests
  │   ├─ Logit
  │   │   ├─ LogitNests, LogitCap, LogitCournot, LogitBLP
  │   │   ├─ Auction2ndLogit, BargainingLogit, MonComLogit
  │   │   └─ CES ── CESNests, CESCournot, Auction2ndCES,
  │   │             BargainingCES, MonComCES
  │   └─ Cournot ── Stackelberg
  └─ Auction2ndCap

Counterfactual ── contains CounterfactualStep objects
CounterfactualPath ── contains model S4 results
```

For example, `CES` extends `Logit` to reuse S4 machinery, and `Cournot`
extends `Bertrand`. Their demand or conduct equations still differ. The map
omits many variants; `methods::showClass()` and `methods::showMethods()` show
the complete, current hierarchy.

## Public methods and dispatch

Inspect the public class contract and available dispatch without printing
whole method bodies:

```{r dispatch}
library(antitrust)
names(methods::getSlots("StructuralFit"))
methods::extends("AntitrustFit", "StructuralFit")
methods::extends("CES", "Logit")
methods::showMethods("simulate", classes = "AntitrustFit")
```

The two `TRUE` values establish inheritance, not economic equivalence.


For result objects, `calcPrices()` and `calcMargins()` are the public price
and margin interfaces. Other important generics include `calcShares()`,
`calcQuantities()`, `elast()`, `diversion()`, `upp()`, `cmcr()`, `CV()`,
`HypoMonTest()`, and `calcDiagnostics()`. Which methods are available depends
on the model class: `elast()` for `Logit`, for instance, uses different demand
equations from `elast()` for `CES`. The help page for each generic gives its
argument and output conventions.

## How model identity selects behavior

The registry behind `supportedModels()` connects a `model_spec()` identity
to a **complete implemented model**: its S4 result class, calibration
constructor, and availability of `calibrate()`, `specify()`, and
`simulate()`. A demand name and conduct name do not create an implementation
merely because each appears elsewhere in the registry. Economic work still
goes through the selected model's constructor and methods.

`respecify()` has a separate, narrower transition registry. It describes
which information can be retained or derived in a target model and which
parameters must be discarded or recomputed. `model_transition()` exposes a
supported source-to-target transition.

The fields accepted by `counterfactual()` are also checked against the
selected model before solving. Entry, quality, capacity, bargaining, and
leadership each require an implementation for that model.

## Obligations of an extension

Suppose a sibling package studies a policy or game outside antitrust's model
registry. It can reuse the fitted-state lifecycle while defining its own
calibration equations, equilibrium solver, and result methods. An extension
can subclass `StructuralFit`, provide `simulate()` and `respecify()` methods
for its fit class, validate its counterfactual fields, and implement
`simulate_steps()` if users should be able to resume paths. The base
`StructuralFit` methods require those implementations; they do not supply
economic behavior for an extension.

| Public contract | Responsibility of the extension |
|:--|:--|
| `StructuralFit` subclass | Store valid model identity, primitives, observations and diagnostics. |
| `simulate()` | Validate the scenario, solve the extension's economics and return its documented result. |
| `respecify()` | State which primitives are retained or reconstructed; never hide a recalibration. |
| `validate_counterfactual()` and `simulate_steps()` | Reject unsupported fields and define how solved state persists when a path resumes. |

See `?"StructuralFit-class"`, `?simulate_steps` and
`?validate_counterfactual` for callable contracts. Existing implementations in
[StructuralFitMethods.R](https://github.com/luciu5/antitrust/blob/master/R/StructuralFitMethods.R)
show dispatch boundaries; an extension must supply its own equilibrium solver.


The sibling packages illustrate the boundary. `vertical` owns vertical
bargaining models; `coordination` owns specialized price-leadership economics;
`trade` adds tariff and quota policy while reusing antitrust; `financial`
owns debt and limited-liability economics; and `antitrustBayes` works with
posterior structural draws. They need not share one registry to share a
clear lifecycle boundary.

Antitrust also owns the public synthetic-market tools:
`synthetic_market()`, `fake_market()`, and `realize_market()`. They separate
market design from its realization under a particular model. An extension
may use the resulting fits, but remains responsible for the validity of its
own economics.

In observed synthetic mode, the neutral design contains product shares,
ownership, positive marginal costs, and one proportional reference-product
margin. It leaves prices unsolved. The model-aware adapter identifies demand
scale and solves equilibrium prices; it rejects registered models whose
additional curvature, capacity, or conduct state is not identified. The
primitives design keeps its separate supplied-price contract.

Use exported functions, documented S4 classes, result generics, and their
stated argument contracts as the integration surface. Internal registry
helpers, promotion functions, solver state, and unnamed attributes can
change without preserving downstream behavior. The help pages for
`StructuralFit`, `AntitrustFit`, `simulate_steps`, and
`validate_counterfactual` describe the callable hooks. Maintainer context
is in the hosted
[architecture notes](https://github.com/luciu5/antitrust/blob/master/ARCHITECTURE.md).
